scope: Model-only frozen-base correction experiment. No new kernel work or application launches.

research_sources.use: Motivates residual stages with original-input access; this implementation does not implement MPRNet, cross-stage feature fusion, or its reported results.
Reviewed iterative answer refinement with latent state; no recursive reasoning or TRM implementation is claimed.

mechanical_tests.scope: One training image, two precisions and one disposable local step. No validation image or saved candidate used.

optimization.loss: L1 + 0.25 * horizontal and vertical gradient L1

training.scope: Frozen first student plus a newly trained full-resolution conditioned residual stage. FP32 first-stage outputs are cached only for fitting. Both stages run during inference; no teacher pixels are inputs.

evaluation.timing_scope: FP16 full-1920x1080 input through both models, intermediate concatenation, and one final grade. No cached first output during inference. Existing fusions reused unchanged.
limitations: No D3D12 integration or game/temporal acceptance. Native runtime is unchanged.
p95 is over ten-replay interval averages, not individual frame tails.
Previously reserved validation images remain excluded from training, but their past scores informed research; this is not an independent final acceptance set.
The second stage adds 4500 updates and 9000 image examples on top of the existing trained base; this is not an equal-total-training-compute architecture comparison.
Pixel metrics do not establish perceptual equivalence. No replacement is accepted.

training_diagnostic.scope: FP32 training-only evaluation; no optimizer step, validation inference or parameter change.
limitations: Scalar variation and alignment describe the correction but do not prove why training converged there.
The head includes 4x4 pixel-shuffle phases; per-channel mean offsets need not be a spatially uniform RGB correction.
No claim that a small correction establishes an irreducible quality limit.

publication_scope: Original source and numeric metadata only. Weights, input/output pixels, activations and vendor implementation stay private.
